The column-sum constraint makes W preserve the tangent direction hyperplane and fixes the induced one-dimensional quotient map. Thus det W gives the oriented tangent determinant, which is positive near I. Each fixed cap contains exactly its own nearby vertex, so the edge ratio product gives its entire volume and smoothness.

The map from an off-diagonal A to an admissible B is bijective by b=−c. J is strictly positive definite, and the equations A_ij+s_i=η_j give orthogonality to every zero-column-sum direction. The constant lift has Q=0. In the zero-sum lift, direct row and column summation gives s_i=−(c₀)_i/(dm−1) and column sums c₀; hence J=m||c₀||²/(dm−1), with the stated positive coefficient.

The two lifts are orthogonal in J and in the column term. Their orthogonality to the zero-column kernel leaves the strictly negative form −J/m there. The column map is onto by the two lifts and its kernel has dimension dm−m=d²−1, accounting for the full physical tangent space.
